description: Injected content that is written to memory and steers future sessions. OWASP lists it as Memory and Context Poisoning (ASI06) in its Top 10 for Agentic Applications.
Who or what produced a memory and through which channel (user, tool, document, assistant), with a reference to the source.
A channel allowed to give the assistant instructions, typically the user about their own preferences. Tools, documents and web content are untrusted.
Every memory and everything derived from it belongs to one owner, and every read is scoped to that owner.
Summaries, extracted facts, embeddings and caches built from memories. They inherit the owner, retention and erasure duties of their sources.
How long a memory may be kept. Expired memories stop being read immediately and are purged on a schedule.
The right to have personal data deleted (GDPR Article 17, the "right to be forgotten"), including copies and derived data.
A record of what was deleted (counts, ids, time) kept for audit, without the deleted content.
